claims.text: Lightweight high-entropy alloys can combine low density with mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Formation of a single-phase BCC solid solution explains the combined low density, strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance.
Controlled cooling and processing can form a single-phase BCC solid solution in a high-entropy alloy.
Selective laser melting or laser powder bed fusion with optimized parameters is an appropriate high-temperature processing condition for forming the proposed structure.
The resulting single-phase BCC solid solution has a uniform distribution of elements.
A single-phase BCC solid solution provides excellent mechanical properties because of uniform elemental distribution and the absence of deleterious phases.
A single-phase BCC solid solution provides corrosion resistance because of uniform elemental distribution and the absence of deleterious phases.
A single-phase BCC solid solution provides high-temperature oxidation resistance because of uniform elemental distribution and the absence of deleterious phases.
The proposed BCC alloy will have improved mechanical properties relative to traditional alloys.
The proposed BCC alloy will have improved corrosion resistance relative to traditional alloys.
The proposed BCC alloy will have improved high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to traditional alloys.
Traditional alloys with similar compositions and processing conditions constitute an appropriate baseline.
The hypothesis should cease to hold when complex compositions or processing produce deleterious phases or non-uniform microstructures.
The exact mechanisms of BCC solid-solution formation and property enhancement are not fully understood.
